Over Arepas and Cachitos, Venezuelans in Madrid Find a Sense of Home

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I stroll down the wide aisles of the sprawling Mercado de Las Maravillas, passing greengrocers with yuca and plantains piled high.
  • I make my way to the prepared-food stalls aisle, where the woman at Buda Bar Delicias Venezolanas draws me in by calling me amor and asking what I’d like to order, reina.
  • The Mercado de Las Maravillas is "where the Venezolanismo here in Madrid started,” restaurant owner Manuel Pérez Álvarez states.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I stroll down the wide aisles of the sprawling Mercado de Las Maravillas, passing greengrocers with yuca and plantains piled high. A digital billboard flashes congratulations for the recent Venezuelan team’s World Baseball Classic win. Nearby, a vendor hawks yellow, blue, and red flags, while signs advertising remittance services to Latin America clutter my sightline. All around me, the Madrid market fills with the round, sing-song accent of Venezuelan Spanish.

I make my way to the prepared-food stalls aisle, where the woman at Buda Bar Delicias Venezolanas draws me in by calling me amor and asking what I’d like to order, reina. The familiar warmth of Latin America—I lived in Mexico before moving to Spain—tears open a pang of nostalgia in my chest. Guests seated at the stainless-steel bar munch on empanadas de carne mechada, continuously reaching for the green, herby salsa guasacaca. “How can it be that they are pumping a million barrels of oil out a day but they cannot fix a single hospital in Caracas?” I overhear another diner say to a friend, discussing the latest spate of frustrations back home.

The Mercado de Las Maravillas is "where the Venezolanismo here in Madrid started,” restaurant owner Manuel Pérez Álvarez states.

Among Madrid’s 130,000-strong Venezuelan diaspora, these conversations are not uncommon. Spain’s Venezuelan population has swollen to almost 700,000 people, making it the largest community outside of the Americas, and a significant portion of the country’s nearly eight million citizens living abroad. Many have fled their homeland amid the economic and political instability that followed Hugo Chavez’s Bolivarian Revolution and continued under Nicolás Maduro’s rule. Ongoing uncertainty continues to drive migration. Unlike other diasporas, Madrid’s Venezuelan population isn’t concentrated in a single neighborhood. Instead, it stretches across the city and spans a broad socioeconomic spectrum, from delivery drivers and financiers to political exiles.

Its food institutions mirror a similar range.

It has been revealed that manuel Pérez Álvarez and his wife Maira María Gómez can pinpoint the moment they decided to open a Venezuelan restaurant in Madrid. The two, who moved to Spain in 1997 after a lifetime in the coastal city of Puerto de La Cruz, had gone to meet friends for Venezuelan empanadas at one of the few spots in town at the time. After waiting 45 minutes for their order in a long line of people hankering for a taste of home, Pérez—a natural entrepreneur—saw opportunity.

Manuel Pérez Álvarez and his wife Maira María Gómez opened El Empanadazo in Madrid nearly a decade ago.

Venezuela's national dish, pabellon criollo—rice, beans, shredded beef, and plantains—is served alongside cachapas, arepas, fried fish, and more.

When they opened El Empanadazo nearly a decade ago, the couple joined the ranks of just a handful of other Venezuelan food joints. They chose to set up shop in the Mercado de Las Maravillas. “It was really where the Venezolanismo here in Madrid started,” Pérez says of the market. In no time, they were serving hearty plates of Venezuela's national dish, pabellon criollo—rice, beans, shredded beef, and plantains—crispy fried whole fish, sweet corn griddled cachapas, arepas, and more.

According to recent reports, “Our restaurant really became a gathering place for Venezuelans. I remember the early days when I was spending more time there, seeing people with tears in their eyes,” Pérez says. “When you’re an immigrant, little things like the taste of home really get to you.”.

Maira María Gómez and her husband Manuel Pérez Álvarez opened El Empanadazo in Madrid nearly a decade ago, there were far fewer Venezuelan restaurants in the city.

Sources indicate that at the time, Venezuelan food wasn’t as easy to find and people went out of their way for it. Today, a quick search for “arepa” on the delivery apps will turn up hundreds of options. “Now there are lots of spots, but we were really pioneers, and it wasn’t even all that long ago,” Pérez says.

According to recent reports, be it Arepa’s Coffee Shop nestled next to the hustle of the Moncloa train and bus station, or the four-location La Arepera, the Insta-famous El Chino Venezolano, or the fast-growing Guasacaca, the country’s gastronomic footprint continues to grow alongside its diaspora in Madrid. At the March 2026 Arepa Fest, a celebration of Venezuelan and Colombian food and culture, in the north edges of Madrid, more than 5,000 people gathered to snack on the region's signature split- and stuffed-cornmeal snack, while the sound system alternated between pumping Venezuelan Merengue and reggaeton.

At Panadería Torrerí, warm pastries like cachitos, a brioche-like crescent roll most typically filled with ham and cheese, and golfeados, spiral pastry dough filled with cheese, keep customers coming back.

Recent findings suggest that A similar fervor can be felt at Panadería Torrerí. By mid-morning, the team is already replenishing their glass case of cachitos, a brioche-like crescent roll most typically filled with ham and cheese, and golfeados, spiral pastry dough filled with cheese, and brushed with panela (unrefined cane sugar) and anise. Regulars grab a table and owner Mara Azuaje, always poised with a “¿Cómo está usted?” swiftly ferries over their order.

Recent findings suggest that azuaje opened her bakery in 2024 to bring traditional Venezuelan pastries to the neighborhood of Barrio de Salamanca. For years, there had been no Venezuelan bakery in the area, despite this upscale neighborhood being nicknamed “Little Caracas” for its substantial diaspora. Today, Panadería Torrerí attracts both affluent property owners alongside motorbike messengers, all looking for a taste of home.

Mara Azuaje opened Panadería Torrerí in the Barrio de Salamanca in 2024.

It has been revealed that azuaje, who came to Spain at 27, knows what they're after. She spent years working odd jobs to save the money needed to open her bakery. “I cleaned homes, worked as a delivery driver, took care of children. I did whatever, but I was always very ambitious,” Azuaje claims. “I wanted to have my own business.”.

Industry observers note that she didn’t understand the exact shape it would take, but her grandmother’s lessons to her as a child around the importance of learning an oficio, a craft, stayed with her. “I was always baking with my grandmother who told me I needed to know how to do something, so I opened a bakery,” she claims. Today, Azuaje is proud to be known across the neighborhood for her homemade bread and her hearty rolled-dough pastries.

Other Venezuelan restaurant owners transitioned into hospitality later in life. At Bea Castelló Castro and Luis Felipe Fossa’s Cafetín, the menu—arepas with chia seeds, shredded chicken, and avocado for breakfast, or creamed curry soup and sweet corn and hearty salads for lunch—carries traces of Venezuela while honoring the other places the couple has called home.

At Cafetín, the menu showcases Venezuelan flavors through a global lens.

Cafetín's arepas are stuffed with chia seeds, shredded chicken, and avocado.

The married pair came to Madrid after a full life in Caracas. “By 2007 Chávez just kept winning and winning, and things were getting worse and worse. It really scared us,” Felipe says. That year was Chávez’s first attempt at constitutional reform to remove presidential term limits and expand state control of the economy. He lost his bid but remained in power and went on to secure reform in 2009. So, when the bank Fossa worked for offered him a job in Zurich, they didn’t hesitate. It was a decision that has led to many years of living abroad.

Bea Castelló Castro and Luis Felipe Fossa say that their Cafetín has become a hub for Venezuelans, who connect over coffee and arepas.

Their clientele reflects a similar worldliness, with Venezuelans who arrived directly from Caracas but also those who have made it here by way of a university in Boston, or lived for years in Miami, Latest York, or London. Cafetín is a meeting point where these Venezuelans intersect, creating a community within a community. As Castelló Castro put it, “empiezas a hacer nexo”—you start to make connections.

Recent findings suggest that recently, I'm told, a couple in a sunlit corner of the cafe started chatting with a man standing at the long bar after hearing him mention Caracas. They began tracing the routes through Miami and Fresh York that had brought them to Madrid. Another day, a college sweatshirt prompted a conversation—and a new friendship. “It’s beautiful to see, especially in difficult moments in Venezuela,” says Castelló Castro.

Sources indicate that back at the Mercado de Las Maravillas, I sit at Buda Bar watching the lunch rush fade, as owner Rebeksa Mouzaber prepares me a sweet-corn crescent-shaped cachapa, its edges lacy from a bed of hot butter on the flattop griddle. A food courier accepts a freshly-made pocket-sized empanada while he scrolls and waits for his order.

In a recent development, venezuelans like coming here because they feel at home—not just in the dishes that are served but also in the way they are asked for, Mouzaber tells me. “We know what it means when they ask for an ñapa (a top-up), just like we know how it feels to be so far away from home.”.

  • President Donald Trump on Thursday shut down his administration’s on-again-off-again talks with Iran, saying he would not seek a deal to formally end the nine-month-old conflict with Tehran.
  • According to recent reports, the possible end of the pursuit of a diplomatic solution came nine days after Trump and congressional Republicans suffered massive losses in the midterm elections.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that president Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance salute during a Wednesday ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery in honor of Veterans Day. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images).

President Donald Trump on Thursday shut down his administration’s on-again-off-again talks with Iran, saying he would not seek a deal to formally end the nine-month-old conflict with Tehran.

According to recent reports, the possible end of the pursuit of a diplomatic solution came nine days after Trump and congressional Republicans suffered massive losses in the midterm elections. House Democrats will have more than 250 seats come January, and Senate Democrats will have at least 55 seats in the Senate — with Alaska’s competitive race still uncalled.

Polls leading up to Election Day and since have shown that a majority of voters, and a sizeable chunk of Trump’s Republican base, felt the Iran conflict was a mistake.

Vice President JD Vance penned a lengthy social media post the day after the election, blaming, in large part, the Iran war for the coast-to-coast Democratic victories. Some GOP lawmakers have also called for an end to the conflict, which drove up fuel and other commodity prices.

Industry observers note that "The reason we lost is the war," Vance wrote the morning after the GOP wipeout. "The president himself noted so last night.".

In a recent development, trump has stated that he agrees with Vance’s assessment but that if he had to decide again whether to join Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in striking Iranian targets, he would reach the same conclusion. On Monday, he told reporters that the Iran war "militarily is effectively over.".

Vance had been Trump’s designated top negotiator in the talks with Iran’s remaining leaders, but the president remarked Thursday on social media that he had ordered his second-in-command to instead “focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.”.

According to recent reports, “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed,” he added. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!".

It has been revealed that the situation along the Strait of Hormuz remains contested and dangerous for commercial vessels, including ones that deliver a large amount of the world’s oil products. Iranian officials contend that they control most of the key waterway.

In a recent development, trump, Vance and other administration officials have said in recent weeks that they were open to continuing talks with Iran, while criticizing Tehran's negotiating tactics. Last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who also is Trump’s national security adviser, told reporters that Iran's latest demands were unreasonable.

Trump’s announcement Thursday could represent his latest way to try assuaging GOP voters, including members of his “Make America Great Again” base. A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after the midterms and released Tuesday revealed that a majority of Republicans (51 percent) want Congress to pass legislation that would end the Iran conflict. Overall, 71 percent of Americans would support such a bill, the survey found.

The conflict was front-and-center during the midterms campaign.

Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers, who lost the Senate race in Michigan to Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, called for the Iran conflict to end "promptly.".

Industry observers note that “Michigan families are struggling with the price of everyday life. Groceries cost too much. We have to bring prices down," Rogers mentioned in one campaign ad.

On Capitol Hill, GOP lawmakers have tried giving Trump cover, while raising some concerns about high gas prices and questioning whether the president and his team have a viable exit strategy.

Industry observers note that as the midterms campaign hit the homestretch in late September, two Iowa Republicans in tight races, Reps. Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks, voted with Democrats on a measure to end the conflict.

“With the negotiating window closed, sustained combat operations now require congressional authorization,” Nunn, an Air Force veteran, wrote on social media. “I will not support another open-ended war.”.

Nunn and Miller-Meeks both lost their seats last week, despite breaking with the president over the war.

Trump’s declaration this week of a military end to the Iran war came more than seven years after he offered some foreshadowing during a June 25, 2019, exchange with this CQ Roll Call reporter in the Oval Office.

Asked that day what his exit strategy would be if war ever broke out with Iran, he said: “You’re not going to need an exit strategy. I don’t do exit strategies.”.

(A very fun part of being in Iceland is passing by every stranger and asking yourself, Is that Björk? Is that Björk? Please be Björk.) Then we got there and went straight into this opaque, milky-blue water; it was kind of like being in a luxurious version of that cloudy bath in Minority Report that [Samantha Morton] lies in. There was a mask bar in the lagoon, where you can apply a silica mud mask, an algae mask, or a mineral mask to your face, and it all felt very thick, goopy, and smooth on the skin. We're Asian and all have eczema, so we experienced a lot of relief afterward. It was very cute seeing families with members of all ages, including my children, wading around the lagoon together with spa masks on their face. Then Sheng—and this is very Sheng—started harvesting the silica off the walls and putting it on his face. Since it was free, we all copied him. I'm not sure if that was good for us or not.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Airline websites are not necessarily badly designed, even though they often feel that way. In many cases, the booking process is doing exactly what it was designed to do: get you focused on the lowest advertised fare before revealing the cost of everything else.

In a recent development, you start with a flight that looks like it costs $400. By the time you add a carry-on bag, choose a seat, and work through the final checkout screens, the total is suddenly $650.

Sources indicate that after more than 18 years of travel to over 130 countries, we still catch ourselves slowing down to double-check airline bookings. The difference now is that we know where the expensive mistakes are usually hiding. We also use flight-search and tracking tools to compare routes and monitor changes. See our guide to the best travel apps for 2026.

It has been revealed that the lowest price on the first screen is rarely enough information to tell you which flight is actually cheapest. You need to compare the complete journey, including baggage, seats, fare restrictions, connections, operating airlines, and the risk involved if something goes wrong.

To avoid costly airline booking mistakes, compare the total price of the journey rather than the advertised base fare. Check the conditions of the exact fare, baggage allowances, operating airline, cabin on every segment, connection times, and whether the flights are issued on one protected ticket.Before paying, compare the flight as a round trip, two one-way tickets, and a multi-city itinerary. Before leaving home, verify your passport, visas or travel authorizations, transit requirements, check-in deadline, and gate-closing time.

These airline booking traps—also common flight-booking mistakes—can turn an apparently cheap ticket into the most expensive option.

One of the first mistakes travellers make is comparing flights by airline logo.

In a recent development, you see the airline you normally use, remember the points sitting in your account, and stop comparing. But loyalty should not convince you to pay hundreds of dollars more for a worse schedule, a more restrictive ticket, or a fare that excludes everything you need.

In a recent development, airline points can still be valuable, especially when you are close to earning useful status or have benefits such as complimentary baggage. But loyalty should be one part of the calculation, not the starting point.

Before choosing an airline, compare:.

The days of automatically paying more because “this is our airline” are over. Loyalty should follow value, not the other way around.

According to recent reports, basic Economy can be a perfectly reasonable fare. The trap is buying it without understanding what has been removed.

It may work well when you are taking a short flight, travelling with only a small personal item, do not care where you sit, and are confident your intends will not change.

The problem is that airline websites normally display the lowest available fare first. Once you are in booking mode, it is easy to select that number and move forward without reading the restrictions.

You may save $40 on the ticket and then spend $85 adding the carry-on bag you needed from the beginning.

Before booking Basic Economy, price the next fare category. A Standard Economy ticket may cost more initially but include a carry-on bag, checked luggage, seat selection, or greater flexibility.

In a recent development, also consider whether seat selection genuinely matters. Travellers with children, mobility considerations, medical needs, or a strong need for an aisle or window seat should include that cost when comparing fares.

Sources indicate that do not buy the lowest number. Buy the fare that includes what you actually need.

In a recent development, airlines do not necessarily sell every Economy Class seat at the same price. Seats are divided into fare classes or pricing tiers, often called fare buckets.

When the cheapest tier sells out, the price can jump even when the aircraft still has many empty seats.

Sources indicate that that is one reason a flight might appear at $480 in the morning and $620 later that day. It does not always mean the plane suddenly filled up. It may mean the least expensive fare class is no longer available.

When you see a noticeable price increase, do not assume you must either pay it immediately or lose the trip.

Start the comparison again and check:.

A competitor may now be cheaper. In other cases, the next fare level may include baggage, seat selection, or flexibility that makes it better value than the stripped-down ticket you were originally considering. A fare jump is a signal to widen the search, not automatically accept the newly introduced price.

For the tools we use to compare dates, airports, and fare changes, see our guide to the best travel apps for finding flights.

The standard airline search box encourages travellers to enter a departure city, destination, outbound date, and return date.

That does not mean a traditional round trip is always the cheapest or most efficient way to book.

Before purchasing an expensive international itinerary, compare it three ways:.

An open-jaw ticket means flying into one city and returning home from another.

For example, if you are travelling through Europe, you might fly into Paris and return from Rome. Even if the airfare is similar to a return ticket from Paris, you could avoid paying for a train or flight back to your starting point. You may also save a hotel night and an entire day of backtracking.

According to recent reports, different airlines can also be used in each direction. One carrier may offer the best outbound flight, while another has a much better return schedule.

Industry observers note that when comparing separate tickets, check baggage fees, fare restrictions, connection risks, and cancellation policies. The goal is not to find the cleverest itinerary. It is to determine which option gives you the best total trip.

With a codeshare flight, the airline selling the ticket may not be the airline flying the plane.

You might purchase the journey through one airline’s website and then arrive at the airport to discover that a partner carrier operates the flight.

Before buying, look for the words “operated by” in the flight details.

Then check the itinerary on both airline websites. Confirm the aircraft, seat map, baggage allowance, terminal, and check-in instructions.

Industry observers note that after booking, make sure you have the operating carrier’s reservation number. The confirmation number issued by the airline selling the ticket may not work on the partner airline’s website.

It has been revealed that codeshares are not automatically bad. They can provide more destinations and useful connections. The problem is that they create a handoff between companies, and that handoff can become confusing when you need assistance.

As we have learned, one of the most expensive sentences in travel can be: “You need to contact the other airline.”.

Mixed-cabin fares are one of the easiest airline traps to miss.

The search result may display a large Premium Economy or Business Class label, making it appear that the entire journey is in the upgraded cabin.

Then you expand the flight details and discover that the 40-minute connection is in Premium Economy while the eight-hour overnight flight is in regular Economy.

We have come close to booking this type of itinerary several times.

In a recent development, before paying, check the cabin listed beside every individual segment. Make sure the premium seat is on the flight where you will actually benefit from it.

Do not assume one premium segment provides premium benefits throughout the trip.

Screenshot the cabin shown for each flight and confirm that it appears correctly in the final reservation. A mixed-cabin fare is only a deal when the upgraded cabin is on the part of the journey that matters.

There is rarely one simple baggage policy that applies to every passenger flying with an airline.

Industry observers note that do not check only the airline’s general baggage page. Open the conditions attached to the specific fare and route you are considering.

According to recent reports, this is especially crucial when connecting from a transatlantic flight to a smaller airline or low-cost carrier within Europe. A bag accepted on the first flight may be too large, too heavy, or not included on the next one.

According to recent reports, A bag fitting inside the overhead compartment does not automatically mean it meets the airline’s rules. Wheels, handles, and outside pockets are normally included when the bag is measured.

Sources indicate that price your luggage before buying the flight. A ticket that appears $30 cheaper can swiftly become more expensive once the necessary baggage is added.

Paying for bags online in advance is also frequently less expensive than waiting until the airport, although the difference varies by airline.

Industry observers note that finally, weigh your suitcase at home using a real scale. Picking it up and declaring that it “feels about 20 kilos” is not a reliable baggage strategy.

Once you know your allowance, follow our two-minute checked-bag routine before handing your suitcase over at the airport.

A self-transfer may be the most expensive mistake in this guide.

Sources indicate that some search and booking sites combine two separate tickets and display them as one journey. Look for warnings such as:.

The critical detail is that the airlines may not recognize the flights as one protected itinerary.

In a recent development, if the first flight is delayed and you miss the second one, the second airline may consider you a no-show. You could lose the remaining flights on that reservation and be forced to purchase a new last-minute ticket.

The first airline may not be responsible for helping because it transported you to the destination shown on its ticket.

A self-transfer can also require you to:.

Leaving the international transit area can also trigger entry or transit requirements that would not apply during a normal airside connection.

Self-transfers can work when you have a long buffer, carry-on luggage, an airport you understand, and enough flexibility to absorb a disruption.

We would not use one when connecting to a cruise, wedding, organized tour, or once-daily long-haul flight.

Always compare the self-transfer price with a protected itinerary. The higher fare may not simply be buying convenience. It may be buying the airline’s responsibility to get you to your final destination.

Airlines can sell a connection that technically meets the airport’s minimum requirements.

That does not necessarily mean it is comfortable, sensible, or suitable for you.

A 45-minute connection at a large international airport might involve:.

If a connection makes you nervous while sitting at home, it will not feel better when you are waiting for the aircraft door to open. Choose connection time based on the consequences of missing the next flight.

In a recent development, A long layover can be inconvenient. A missed connection can cost a full day or derail the entire trip.

Recent findings suggest that we use third-party flight sites for research. They are useful for comparing airlines, dates, and routing options.

Buying through one is a separate decision.

Sources indicate that A third-party fare may be genuinely cheaper, but make sure you are comparing the same product. It could involve:.

The biggest issue normally appears when the schedule changes or the flight is cancelled.

In a recent development, the airline may tell you to contact the firm that issued the ticket. The booking company may then tell you that only the airline can resolve the flight.

Before buying, find the itinerary through the search site and compare it directly with the airline. When the price difference is small, booking with the airline may be worth it for easier communication during disruptions.

Recent findings suggest that also check the payment currency. Some booking sites offer to convert the total into your home currency. This feels convenient but may include a less favourable exchange rate.

According to recent reports, when your credit card does not charge a foreign transaction fee, paying in the original currency may be less expensive. Compare the final converted amount and check your card’s fees rather than choosing a currency based on familiarity.

Some of the most expensive travel problems do not happen during booking. They happen at the airport after your hotel, tour, rental car, or cruise has already been paid for.

A valid passport may not be enough to enter your destination or transit through a connecting country.

Depending on your nationality, route, and destination, you may need:.

It has been revealed that A passport can be valid on your departure date and still fail to meet the destination’s entry requirements. Complicated connections are also a good reason to review our international travel safety tips before departure.

It has been revealed that names matter too. The name on your airline ticket should match your passport and any visa or travel authorization. Do not assume that a nickname or commonly used name will be accepted.

Before an international trip, take five minutes to verify:.

Canadian travellers should verify current destination-specific requirements using official government travel advisories and the relevant embassy or immigration authority, since entry and transit rules can change.

Recent findings suggest that five minutes at home can save the entire trip at the airport. For our complete pre-departure routine, read our travel safety checklist for 2026.

Industry observers note that departure time is when the aircraft is scheduled to leave. It is not the time you should arrive at the gate.

Boarding begins earlier, and the gate closes before departure. The exact cutoff depends on the airport, airline, route, and destination.

Once the gate is closed, seeing the aircraft through the terminal window will not save your seat.

It has been revealed that if you miss the flight, the cost may extend far beyond a replacement ticket. You might also lose:.

Build your airport schedule backward from the airline’s check-in, baggage-drop, boarding, and gate-closing deadlines.

Industry observers note that check current security conditions using the airport’s official app or website, but do not treat an estimated wait time as a guarantee. Add time for airport parking, shuttle transportation, baggage drop, security, passport control, terminal changes, and finding the gate.

Sources indicate that it is better to have extra time near the gate than to spend the start of your trip running through an airport while your name is being called over the loudspeaker. Arriving early does not help much if your carry-on slows you down at screening. Read our airport security tips and common mistakes before packing.

Before confirming a flight, we recommend checking the entire itinerary one final time.

The best defence against airline booking traps is not a secret search setting or complicated flight hack. It is slowing down long enough to compare the complete journey.

All 12 of these traps work best when travellers are rushing.

We see a low fare, get excited about the trip, and want to finish before the number changes. The booking process then reveals the bags, seats, restrictions, connections, and other costs after we have already become emotionally committed to the flight.

Recent findings suggest that the cheapest flight is not necessarily the one with the lowest number on the first screen. It is the flight that gets you to your destination without surprise charges, unrealistic connections, or an expensive problem at the airport.

Recent findings suggest that after more than 18 years of travelling, experience has not made us immune to booking mistakes. It has simply taught us when to stop, reopen the details, and check everything one more time.

According to recent reports, take five minutes before pressing confirm. Those five minutes could save hundreds of dollars—or save the entire trip.

Windstar Cruises has announced its Thankful for Travel 2026 promotion, featuring added value on more than 600 voyages through March 2028.

For bookings made from November 18 to December 2, 2026, on select voyages departing through March 31, 2028, guests get a complimentary All-Inclusive package valued at $99 per guest, $300 onboard credit per stateroom and reduced deposits of $150 per person.

Featured destinations include Europe, Greece, Iceland and Tahiti, as well as voyages aboard the newly introduced Star Explorer, debuting in December 2026.

Select specialty voyages and Star Collector itineraries are excluded from the offer.

“The holidays are a natural time for travelers to start thinking about where they want to go next, and travel advisors play such an vital role in turning those ideas into memorable experiences,” mentioned Janet Bava, chief commercial officer of Windstar Cruises.

“With Thankful for Travel, we’re giving our partners a compelling opportunity to help clients initiative ahead, with meaningful added value and exciting options across Europe, Tahiti and beyond.”.

For a particularly memorable start to 2027, guests can ring in the fresh year aboard the 224-guest Star Explorer on its nine-night maiden voyage roundtrip from Barcelona on December 28.

Other holiday sailings include Windstar’s 2026 Christmas cruises sailing either French Polynesia or Panama and Costa Rica.

French Polynesia itineraries will be operated by two ships in 2027 as the Wind Star is set to join the Star Breeze in March.

Apart from this, guests can opt for Windstar’s year-round Mediterranean voyages to discover the Greek Isles or go farther north and explore Iceland and Northern Europe.

Intervine has added Susurrus Sparkling Teas to its portfolio, expanding its premium non-alcoholic offerings for onboard programs.

According to a press release, Susurrus brings a fine-wine perspective to organic sparkling tea, with an emphasis on origin, vintage and terroir, resulting in a premium experience with the same sophistication as wine.

“The world of tea is just as vast and fascinating as the world of wine. Sparkling tea is its own fresh, distinct category that can bring the best of these two worlds together,” said Ellison Wofford, founder of Susurrus Sparkling Teas.

“I crafted Susurrus to be appealing to a broad audience because you can enjoy it for what it is—single-origin, single-cultivar, organic tea—rather than for what it lacks: alcohol. I am beyond thrilled to partner with Intervine. Together, we will provide a healthy, refreshing, and elegant option to guests of all kinds while traveling.”.

Unlike dealcoholized wine, Susurrus is inherently non-alcoholic, with tea leaves cold-steeped instead fermented, and the finished teas carbonated at pressure levels comparable to Champagne and sparkling wine.

There are at the moment two varieties: Magnolia Oolong and Osmanthus Golden Tip, both of which come from hand-harvested teas that Wofford directly imports from China.

Designed to be served chilled in a flute or white wine glass, the teas offer their own distinctive flavor profiles and are designed to complement food, providing an alternative to wine.

“I was blown away the first time I tasted Ellison’s lovely creations,” said Jonjie Lockman, CEO of Intervine.

It has been revealed that “‘Champagne’s sober sister,’ as we like to refer to it, provides sophistication, depth of flavors, and complexity in abundance. The Intervine team is proud to bring this special beverage to our airline, airport, and cruise line customers from across the world.”.

Former Maine Gov. Paul LePage, fifth from right, joins incoming members Thursday for their freshman class photo on the House steps outside the Capitol. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Paul LePage, the former Maine governor who once said he was “Donald Trump before Donald Trump,” is heading to Congress.

In a recent development, the Associated Press called the race for the open 2nd District on Thursday after the Maine Secretary of State’s office tabulated the votes under the state’s ranked choice voting system. LePage ended up ahead of Democratic state Auditor Matt Dunlap 50.8 percent to 49.2 percent.

It has been revealed that dunlap had already conceded the race to LePage, who will succeed retiring Democratic Rep. Jared Golden in the sprawling district, which includes much of Maine outside the Portland and Augusta areas.

According to recent reports, “Paul LePage is already hard at work for the people of Maine attending Congressional orientation, meeting with national leaders, and making it clear the political parties need to work together for the American people,” Brent Littlefield, a senior adviser to LePage, said in a statement Thursday. “As Paul said, he will work with anyone, regardless of Party, to put Maine first.”.

LePage’s win is a glimmer of good news for Republicans, who saw massive losses across the country in last week’s midterm elections. He is one of three Republicans, along with Texas’ Jace Yarbrough and Tennessee’s Brent Taylor, to have flipped a House seat, although Maine’s 2nd District is the only one of the three that wasn’t redrawn to favor the GOP.

In a recent development, lePage’s win also means that at least one Republican will continue to represent New England in Congress, taking up the mantle from Maine Sen. Susan Collins, who lost her own reelection bid last week.

In a recent development, golden, who was first elected in 2018, had been a top Republican target throughout his time in Congress. But the lawmaker, known for bucking his party, proved difficult to unseat in the past two election cycles.

“I also know a thing or two about winning in tough circumstances. So, I know you have to tip your hat to Paul LePage for winning in the midst of this Blue Tsunami,” Golden remarked in a social media post last week.

Dunlap initially rolled out his campaign as a primary challenge to Golden in the fall of 2025, only for the congressman to announce his retirement a month later. Dunlap went on to win a four-way contest for the Democratic nomination.

Airlines measure lithium-ion battery size in watt-hours, written as Wh.

The 100 Wh rule matters most for large laptop power banks, professional camera gear, video equipment and drone batteries.

A typical 10,000 mAh power bank is often around 37 Wh. A 20,000 mAh power bank is often around 74 Wh. Larger power banks can get close to the limit, so check before you pack.

Do not travel with a battery that is swollen, cracked, leaking, unusually hot, damaged or recalled.

A swollen power bank is not “probably fine.” It is a damaged battery and should be taken to an appropriate recycling or disposal location.

It has been revealed that before flying with an older power bank, check the model number and look for current recall notices from the manufacturer or your government recall site. Some recalled power banks may be prohibited onboard entirely.

If a battery looks questionable, leave it at home. Replacing a charger is cheaper than dealing with a safety incident at the airport.

If a battery or device becomes hot, starts swelling, smokes, sparks or smells strange during a flight, tell the cabin crew immediately.

Do not put it in the overhead bin. Do not hide it in a bag. Do not take it to the washroom. Cabin crew are trained to respond to battery incidents, but they need to know right away.

Sources indicate that the goal is not to handle the problem yourself. The goal is to alert the people trained to deal with it.

Before leaving for the airport, do this quick check:.

This takes less than two minutes and can prevent a pulled bag, confiscated item or airport delay.

Before you check a suitcase or hand over a carry-on at the gate, make sure:.

Before you check any bag, open it and look for batteries.

Power banks, portable chargers, spare batteries and removable lithium batteries stay with you in the cabin. Phones, laptops, tablets and cameras are usually safer in your carry-on. If your carry-on gets taken at the gate, remove your battery pouch before the bag goes underneath the plane.

The goal is not to stop travelling with electronics. The goal is to stop packing them on autopilot.

A two-minute battery check before every flight can save your bag, your gear and possibly your travel day.

Breaking: How I Got My Visa to France

📅 16 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1969 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve been in love with France ever since my first trip to Bordeaux in 2010.
  • Recent findings suggest that but that love became an obsession when, after Bordeaux, I stepped out of the Paris metro and onto the Champs-Élysées.
  • Since then, Paris has had a firm grip on my heart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been in love with France ever since my first trip to Bordeaux in 2010. Friends I had met back in Thailand revealed me around the area and introduced me to French culture. It was my first time in France and I loved the food, the wine, and the people.

Recent findings suggest that but that love became an obsession when, after Bordeaux, I stepped out of the Paris metro and onto the Champs-Élysées. The lights, the energy, the mystique! There was magic in the air. I felt like I had known the city my entire life and I was simply returning home.

Since then, Paris has had a firm grip on my heart. Over the years, I spent countless visits exploring France and Paris in particular. I’ve run tours in the city and I spent a few months living there in 2019.

Last August, after yet another sojourn, I thought to myself, “What if I moved back?”.

I was growing a bit tired of the NYC dating scene, the rising cost of living, and felt like, creatively, I was in a rut. With AI coming for creators like me and the industry changing, I was a little lost on what, career-wise, would come next.

And Paris seemed like the best place to go.

Industry observers note that it’s cheaper than NYC, I had friends there already, I’ve always wanted to learn French, it would make a great base for exploring Europe, and I could start writing my next book there. There’s nothing like a change in scenery to get the creativity flowing!

But the question remained: how do you move to France?

After all, they don’t have a digital nomad visa, and you’re limited to three months if you visit on your regular Schengen tourist visa.

Industry observers note that well, it turns out that it’s not actually that hard. (And while I can only speak for Americans, I suspect the criteria are similar for Canadians, Aussies, Kiwis, and other “developed” nations.).

If you want to move to France, you have four main options:.

The student visa is pretty straightforward. You need to enroll in a full-time university program and show you have enough funds to support yourself (around 600 Euros per month). A friend is currently there on this visa, as she is doing a nine-month intensive French program to become fluent. You still have to apply for the visa, but if you’re enrolled in an accredited school, you’ll likely get approved. Another benefit to this visa is that you can work part-time on it!

But this visa is contingent on being in school, so if you leave or quit, it’s voided. However, when you are done, you can change this to a “job seeker” visa, which can give you up to another six months in France (or more depending on how long your program was).

Industry observers note that I thought about applying for the entrepreneur visa, but the application process is pretty complex and can take months to be approved. You have to set up your business in France — and that is a lot of paperwork. You have to show that your business makes money, has clients (at least one of them being French), and can support you full-time (you have to make at least the French minimum wage). They will scrutinize your assets and financials a lot and you’ll need to register your business in France and pay French taxes.

Additionally, France offers a talent visa. If you’re an expert in your field (with verifiable accreditations and accolades), this could be a good visa to apply for, especially if you initiative to stay in France for a long time and want to physically work there. But, again, you’ll need to have some source of income and plan to do physical business in France. If you’re not an academic but someone in the arts, you have to show how you are going to add to the “culture of France” in some way.

While I would meet the requirements for both those visas, the process for either would have been time-consuming, and, since I’m not sure France is going to be my forever home, I decided not to go through that process.

So I went with the long-term visitor visa, officially called VLS-TS visiteur. This allows me to stay up to 12 months in France and is renewable in the country. It does come with a lot of restrictions, however: I can’t physically work here and I am not allowed into the French social welfare system.

In a recent development, it’s also the visa a lot of Americans (and most retirees) are coming in on. If you have passive income or retirement savings and just want to live in France, this is a good option for you. It allows you to set up a bank account and it can be renewed pretty much indefinitely.

The paperwork for this visa (which I’ll get into in a bit) essentially comes down to whether or not you can support yourself. French authorities want to make sure you won’t be a burden on the system.

In a recent development, my biggest question centered around whether or not I could “work” on this visa. A lot of creators and digital nomads are applying for — and getting — this visa.

But remember: you aren’t allowed to work on this visa so how are you going to work if you can’t work?

So let me take a moment to talk about “work” from a legal standpoint.

As I mentioned, there’s no digital nomad visa that allows you to work in France. And the French tax office remarked last July that remote work is considered taxable — but there are no official laws that say so. That’s just their opinion and there’s been no progress in codifying that opinion. In fact, my visa doesn’t even come with a tax number, so I can’t be taxed. I couldn’t pay taxes even if I wanted to.

The visa office asks how you’ll support yourself when you are in France and one of the sources of income they accept is “income from work.” I was very open that my means of support would be the income from this blog and my books.

The system there really hasn’t caught up to remote work. It still defines “work” as something you do physically that could take away a job from a French person.

So could I run walking tours in Paris? Nope. Could you work at a café? Nope.

In a recent development, but does writing this blog post count as work? After all, no one is paying for it. It’s a free resource. Does going to a café to work on the next great American novel count? What about my weekly newsletter that has affiliate links (that generate income) in it? Is writing that considered work?

The gray area is considerable, so the best thing to do is to talk to a lawyer. I recommend Daniel Tostado (yes, that’s his real name), one of the biggest American-French immigration lawyers in Paris. He has a huge law firm and regularly meets with government officials to clarify the rules on this. He gave me some solid advice.

For this long-term visitor visa, the application process is pretty easy. You go to the French government website, fill out your application, take the application number to the TLScontact website, and make an appointment. (France outsources the appointment process to this tech giant, which then sends everything to the French consulate for approval.).

The main things you’ll want to demonstrate are that you have accommodation for 90 days on your application and enough income to support yourself. They just want to make sure you aren’t going to be a burden on the system. I went overboard. Here’s what I brought to my appointment:.

It has been revealed that I didn’t need the second bank account, tax returns, or W-2 (they weren’t required) but the woman at the appointment said the more proof you had the better and it wouldn’t hurt. And another friend who got this visa didn’t bring anything beyond what was asked in the application form. But I wanted to take no chances!

At the appointment, the staff double-checks your paperwork, takes your biometric data, collects the fees, and then sends your passport to the embassy for processing. Officially, it takes up to 15 days to process your visa, but everyone I know seems to get it back within a week.

Recent findings suggest that the worst part was not knowing if you are approved until your passport is returned. While you can track the progress of your application, you don’t know the verdict until your passport is back in your hands. While I was waiting (and anxiously spiraling), I looked on Reddit and found that most denials were for lack of income or challenges with their accommodation, which seem to be the two most important things to have perfect on your application.

Once you get your visa back, you can enter France any time after the start date. After you enter, you have 90 days to register your visa with the state (they give you a little QR code with instructions). This allows you to “officially” be on this long-term visa. (It’s a more paperwork kind of thing.).

Once that is done, there’s nothing else to do and you can stay in France (and Europe) until your visa expires!

So, if you’re considering moving to France, these are your options. But, as always, I’m not a lawyer and this is not legal advice. In regard to work and other issues or questions, it’s important that you seek legal counsel and get their expert opinion!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Gemini, a 960-passenger ship formerly operated by Miray Cruises, was reportedly sold in an auction held by Greek authorities on November 18, 2026.

According to financial and business news portal New Money, the ship, which was auctioned to settle debts of its former operator and owner, was acquired by an undisclosed buyer.

The 3,806,562.75 euro paid is slightly higher than the auction’s opening bid, which was set at Gemini’s project scrap value of 3,805,462 euros.

Newly introduced Money mentioned that four companies expressed interest in acquiring the 19,093-ton vessel that was originally built in 1992 for Crown Cruise Line.

As previously reported by Cruise Industry News, the auction was originally scheduled to take place in late October but was later postponed due to an objection filed by DenizBank with the Single-Member Court of First Instance of Piraeus.

The Turkish bank opposed the initial auction, claiming that the vessel is worth more than its scrap value thanks to 2025 repairs and asking the authorities to increase the opening bid price to 14 million euros.

Greek authorities seized the ship in Karystos earlier this year over a monetary claim of approximately 22,772 euros, followed by its towing to the Port of Elefsis, near Piraeus, in late June, where it remains docked.

The Gemini was last in service in 2025, offering a series of short cruises to Turkey and the Greek Islands.

It was scheduled to operate a cruise program in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Black Sea this summer, but the deployment was cancelled due to Miray’s financial problems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New England is the ancestral home of moderate Republicans, from the Saltonstalls to the Bushes, whose fiscal conservatism and social moderation defined the national GOP for decades.

Industry observers note that last week, Yankee Republicans suffered a near-total wipeout. Maine’s Susan Collins, Upcoming England's last GOP senator, lost her seat to Democrat Troy Jackson, leaving former Maine Gov. Paul LePage, who just won a House seat, as the lone Republican headed to Congress from the region. (The picture was a bit brighter at the state level, where GOP Govs. Phil Scott of Vermont and Kelly Ayotte of New Hampshire were both reelected.).

Sources indicate that one Republican operative sees a path out of the wilderness in a post-Trump era. In an opinion piece in The Boston Globe, consultant Kristin Tate urged Fresh England Republicans to focus on fiscal discipline and recognize that “independence from national party leadership can be a political asset, not an act of betrayal.”.

After all, as the midterm election results remind us, no political realignment lasts forever.

Recent findings suggest that three decades ago, there were plenty of moderate Democrats from Southern states serving in Congress, governor’s mansions and even the White House. But in the years since Bill Clinton's exit from the political stage, Democrats have largely written off the South.

Sources indicate that which is partly why last week’s Democratic wins in the Carolinas, Georgia and, perhaps most notably, Mississippi were so stunning. All the elements that powered the party to victory nationally – disillusionment with Donald Trump, a rise in economic populism and hunger for change – played a role in the South as well.

But other factors were unique to a region that has seen renewed attempts to dilute Black political power with the redrawing of House districts to favor the GOP.

The Republican redistricting gambit in Southern states did not fully yield the desired results and seems to have helped galvanize Black voters and their allies, powering Democrats to unlikely victories.

It’s too soon to say whether the GOP’s reduced hold on the South represents a temporary blip or an enduring shift.

But Joe Trippi, a longtime Democratic strategist who advised candidates in Alabama and Florida this year, has a message for his party: “We need to invest in the South.”.

#MSSEN: Democrat Scott Colom defeated GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction and the first in his party to win a Senate seat in the Magnolia State since 1982.

In a recent development, tar Heel tidal wave: Democrats in North Carolina have picked up at least five House seats, a striking development given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Prior to last week, no House Republican incumbent had lost a general election in the state since Republicans won control of the redistricting process more than a decade ago. And the Democratic gains could grow: In the 5th District, former journalist Chuck Hubbard narrowly leads 11-term Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx, and in the 3rd District, former state Rep. Raymond Smith holds a razor-thin edge over Republican Rep. Greg Murphy. The Associated Press had not called either race at publication time, though Murphy has conceded.

Sources indicate that republicans pick campaign chairs: Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack will be the chairs of Republicans’ respective campaign committees for the 2028 cycle. GOP lawmakers held their leadership elections Tuesday, as our colleagues Savannah Behrmann and John T. Bennett reported. Senate Republicans are sticking with South Dakota’s John Thune to lead them in the next Congress, while House Republicans picked former Freedom Caucus Chair Jim Jordan as their leader.

It has been revealed that redistricting doubts: Maryland could be getting a new congressional map after voters approved a constitutional amendment that would clear the way for new lines in 2028. Our colleague Victor Feldman has more on the result and other election-related ballot measures across the country. But it’s not clear how many other states may look to redistrict next cycle after Republican efforts over the past 18 months largely didn’t pay off in last week’s elections.

Run the table: With Rep. Darren Soto winning a sixth term in Florida, no Democratic incumbent lost reelection to a Republican this year. Soto’s win in a redrawn district also meant that Florida Democrats defended all four seats the GOP had targeted under a new congressional map.

Sources indicate that california contest: Rep. Ken Calvert defeated fellow Republican Rep. Young Kim in a rare member-versus-member contest for a redrawn Southern California seat that turned acrimonious. Republicans are poised to hold just four House seats in the Golden State after Democrats made good on five pickup opportunities under a newly introduced congressional map.

Cheesecake Factory caucus: The latest episode of the Political Theater podcast, hosted by Roll Call editor-in-chief Jason Dick, breaks down how candidates in both parties fared in counties where The Cheesecake Factory operates, after the popular chain restaurant became something of a side character in the closing weeks of the midterm campaign.

Back to school: Newly elected members of Congress are on Capitol Hill this week for freshman orientation, an experience Massachusetts Rep.-elect Dan Koh told our colleague Nina Heller is “like high school – but it’s fun high school.” The incoming lawmakers took their class photo Thursday morning and will get to pick their Capitol Hill offices after next week’s famed lottery, Nina writes.

Tracking the count: As of 4:30 p.m. Eastern time Thursday, House Democrats had flipped 44 seats, while Republicans had picked up three. Twelve races remain uncalled, including a pair in Louisiana that will be decided by December runoffs. On the Senate side, Democrats have flipped eight seats, with only Alaska’s race still undecided.

According to recent reports, guv patch: Democrats flipped at least five governorships last week and will hold a majority of governor’s mansions next year. Two gubernatorial races remain uncalled by the AP: Kansas, where Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher is narrowly ahead of Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson, and Alaska, where Democratic former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is just below the 50 percent threshold to win the election outright. In territorial elections, Republicans flipped the governor’s office in Guam while voters in the Northern Mariana Islands will pick their next governor in a Nov. 20 runoff.

Sources indicate that #TNSEN: Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who was elected Tennessee governor last week, is poised to pick her Senate successor. According to the Nashville Banner, the short list includes Knox County Mayor Glenn Jacobs, a former professional wrestler, Reps. Tim Burchett and Chuck Fleischmann, and Tennessee Deputy Gov. Stuart McWhorter.

2028 on the brain: A handful of House Democrats are already considering 2028 Senate bids, according to Axios, including Kansas’ Sharice Davids, North Carolina’s Don Davis and Pennsylvania’s Chris DeLuzio.

Senator Morrison? Minnesota Rep. Kelly Morrison is earning buzz as a potential appointee to fill the Senate seat that Democrat Amy Klobuchar is vacating to become governor, Semafor reports. House Democrats aren’t likely to be as concerned about open seats as their Republican counterparts were in recent years, given the size of the incoming Democratic majority.

Sources indicate that AOC’s future: Progressive activists have released a latest organization to encourage New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028. Meanwhile, Axios reports that Ocasio-Cortez has parted ways with the digital fundraising firm she’s worked with for several years and has brought on the same firm that Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders used during his two presidential campaigns.

In a recent development, women lead: Shirley Emehelu is Upcoming Jersey’s new lieutenant governor after Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill picked her to succeed Dale Caldwell, who resigned in September amid sexual harassment allegations and other ethical lapses. New Jersey is now one of five states to have women in both the governor’s and lieutenant governor’s offices, along with Massachusetts, Arkansas, Iowa and Virginia. Iowa will come off the list next year after an all-male Democratic ticket swept this year’s gubernatorial race, though five other states elected women to both offices last week.

In a recent development, congress will once again be filled with losers – i.e, new members who have lost previous bids for elected office. Roll Call elections analyst Nathan L. Gonzales of Inside Elections returns to his biennial tradition as he runs down the latest list of “losers.”.

Recent findings suggest that ducking the wave: Democrats notched major wins in unexpected places, but one state grew redder after last week’s elections. The Fresh York Times checks in with voters in South Dakota, where the GOP won all nine statewide elections.

It has been revealed that here come the MBAs: Democrats with corporate connections were among the winners in last week’s elections, countering the idea that candidates with serious business credentials have struggled within the party, The Wall Street Journal reports. The field of 19 winners with M.B.A. degrees includes Costco board member Helena Buonanno Foulkes, who won the Rhode Island governor’s race, and Paige Cognetti, a Goldman Sachs alum who flipped a House seat in Pennsylvania.

Recent findings suggest that how Ricketts did it: Nebraska Sen. Pete Ricketts’ election night success was one of the few bright spots for the GOP. Ricketts fended off a challenge from independent Dan Osborn by painting him as a Democrat, questioning his authenticity and highlighting leaked audio of his comments denigrating Trump voters, writes the Nebraska Examiner.

It has been revealed that was it necessary? California redrew its congressional map to favor Democrats in response to Texas taking a similar step to boost the GOP. But some are questioning whether the state needed to cast aside its independent redistricting commission to rejigger the lines, given the scale of Democrats’ wins. “What they were literally saying is, ‘Let’s undo democracy to protect democracy,’” Lincoln Project co-founder Mike Madrid told CalMatters. “There’s something very Orwellian about it.”.

Song of the cycle: The New York Times reviews “Talafreako,” an unlikely viral anthem celebrating the newly elected Democratic senator from Texas.

History does rhyme: An opinion piece in The (Charleston) Post & Courier argues that the win by Democratic Sen.-elect Annie Andrews is the latest in a long line of cases in which South Carolina voters bucked the idea of party bosses picking their leaders.

The man behind the grill: The Latest York Times profiles Russ Hudson, the Mississippi man in Colom’s now-legendary “Pick another protein” ad.

That was the last time Democrats won 11 House seats in North Carolina.

In a recent development, as of Thursday afternoon, they appear on track to match that number. They’ve already won nine seats – a mark they last cleared in the 1982 midterms – and they’re narrowly ahead in two more races.

If those leads hold, Democrats' 11-member delegation would look much different than the one sworn in some 66 years ago in 1961. Tar Heel Democrats taking office in January would include four women, six Black members and one Hispanic member.

Their 11 representatives (out of 12) in the 87th Congress were all white men who consistently voted to uphold racial segregation and oppose major federal civil rights legislation.

Latest Update: Don’t Visit Ko Lipe

📅 23 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1245 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After 19 years, I finally went back to Ko Lipe, the Thai island I spent close to a month on in 2006.
  • Sources indicate that there was much to do here but that was the point.
  • It was paradise – and a place a lot of people got stuck.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 19 years, I finally went back to Ko Lipe, the Thai island I spent close to a month on in 2006. Back then, it was one of those super off-the-beaten-path destinations that few but the most intrepid travelers visited, where electricity only ran a few hours a day, basic bungalows right on the beach cost something like $2 USD, and there really was a last boat for the season.

Sources indicate that there was much to do here but that was the point. You hung out on the beach, read a book, went snorkeling, went back to the beach, drank beers at the one beach bar on the island, rotated meals between the five restaurants there, and went to bed early.

It was paradise – and a place a lot of people got stuck. Days easily turned into weeks here.

If you asked me what the highlight of all my travels was, I would be the time I spent on Ko Lipe. I made incredible friends, lounged around, got to know the locals, learned a bit of Thai, and, overall, lived that idyllic backpacker life we all dream about.

Over the years, I’ve avoided going back to Ko Lipe because the memory of my time there is so strong that I didn’t want to ruin it. Any re-visit would simply be trying to recreated a magic that couldn’t be recreated because the people that it special wouldn’t be there. I’d be chasing travel ghosts. And, since I know my sleepy paradise has been developed greatly over the years, I was also too afraid seeing that would make me sad.

Tourism in Thailand tends toward the unsustainable. No island really develops in a good way. It’s all build, build, build.

And I didn’t want to see my Ko Lipe like that.

But as I was planning my recent trip through Southeast Asia, returning to Ko Lipe made sense. I was heading down the Indian Ocean side of Thailand on my way into Malaysia and I’d pass by it.

And, since I was looking for a lively place for Upcoming Year’s Eve, it seemed liked the best choice. I knew there would be travelers there and there were no other nearby islands that would work, especially since Ko Lipe has a boat to Langkawi, which was my next stop.

And I’m sad to report that Ko Lipe took the Ko Phi Phi model of tourism and is now extremely overdeveloped.

Industry observers note that most of the island is now paved over, the old dirt footpaths having become concrete for the cars and construction trucks. Swaths of palm trees are now the sites of high-end resorts with pools (on an island with no natural water supply). Construction of more resorts continues at a fast pace. The coral around the island is dying, a victim of all the boats, anchors, pollution, and overfishing. Beaches are now lined with boats, their exhaust spilling into the ocean, leaving a shiny film you can see as you swim. And the restaurants cater to tourists looking for bad Western food, not great Thai cuisine.

According to recent reports, the island’s boom has displaced many locals, who were forced to sell to mainland developers, and much of the island’s workforce is now from the mainland. They see little of the benefits this tourism boom.

So lies Ko Lipe, another victim of Thailand’s all too common overdevelopment and exploitation of limited resources.

It has been revealed that I met lots of people there who loved the island. If it’s your first time, I can see why you would love it. After all, the area is postcard perfect, the water is perfectly an azure blue, the sand is a beautiful white, and since you’re surrounded by a national park, a lot of tours take you to some secluded islands.

And, in comparison to Ko Phi Phi, Krabi, or Phuket, it is less developed so I can’t fault someone stepping here for the first time going “wow!”.

But, as I reflect on the island and its overdevelopment, I have come to the same conclusion I have about Ko Phi Phi: people shouldn’t visit.

I’m not against growth, but I’m against this kind of growth. It’s not sustainably managed and going there will only tax the island’s limited resources even further. You can’t put the genie back in the bottle and no local is going to say “sure, I’ll stay broke so you can an idealized vision of the world.”.

And, with so many other islands to visit that are well managed (Ko Lanta, Ko Jum, and Ko Mook, to name three nearby), I think you should skip Ko Lipe.

A visit there will only make things worse.

Sources indicate that it pains me to say that, because it was such a beautiful place, and my original visit had a huge impact on my life. But if we’re going to be good stewards and travelers, sometimes you just have to say enough is enough.

And Ko Lipe is a place where enough is enough.

Go somewhere else that is better managed.

Because your choices do have an impact.

In a recent development, riding elephants in Thailand went away when consumers became more conscious of it. Eco lodges got substantial because of consumers. Overtourism is talked about by consumers as much as it is by locals.

Maybe if enough people start to do something, Ko Lipe will change.

But, at the very least, by not going you are at least no contributing to the problem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., talks with reporters in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.

Industry observers note that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., stated Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out.

It has been revealed that “I know it’s going to be my main push,” he said. “I have to work with colleagues to try to find some language that works. And I’m not there yet, but I’ve told everybody that’s an opportunity.”.

In a recent development, democratic Sens. Michael Bennet of Colorado, Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, Tammy Duckworth of Illinois and independent Bernie Sanders of Vermont released a statement Thursday that they would oppose any deal that does not include “language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.”.

Recent findings suggest that “When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war,” the senators said. “It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”.

It is unlikely that Republicans, who are in control of both chambers of Congress until January, not to mention the Oval Office beyond that, would agree to such a deal.

House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., stated earlier this week that “a Republican Congress is not going to send bills to a Republican president that he's going to veto.”.

While ending the war is a top priority of Democrats as they take back power in the new Congress, insisting on doing so this year could lead to a Christmas-time partial government shutdown. If a shutdown starts after Dec. 11, it’s possible it would still be ongoing when Democrats take control of both chambers in January.

But some Democrats appeared to still be weighing how rapidly to push for a cutoff of war funding.

Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash, said that whether or not Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in his job, “we’re still going to have language stopping this war.”.

She was coy on whether that fight would take place on the anticipated continuing resolution in December or wait until next year when Democrats take back power, saying that lawmakers are “looking at all options.”.

Industry observers note that democrats are committed to ending the "reckless and costly war of choice in Iran," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., mentioned Thursday. He deferred to House Appropriations ranking member Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., "to see what’s possible in advance of Dec. 11" in talks with the other top appropriators.

In a recent development, "I don’t want to get out ahead of Congresswoman DeLauro, but House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine. to Pete Hegseth’s war machine, over in the Middle East," Jeffries mentioned.

It’s not clear how long a potential continuing resolution would last, and DeLauro noted earlier this week that she wants it to be as short as possible.

The Office of Management and Budget has not yet submitted “anomalies” — changes to the current spending levels to be included in the continuing resolution — to Congress.

Sources indicate that the administration is considering options including a stopgap bill that would run through March, sources familiar with the talks said. But no decision on the timing covered by the anomalies has been made.

Aris Folley, Jacob Fulton and Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

💡 Key Takeaways
